title: ECoG hemispheric asymmetry during reaching (Merrick et al. 2022): authors' 1000 Hz intracranial exports with reach kinematics
description: Intracranial electrocorticography (ECoG) recordings from six patients with intractable epilepsy, three with left-hemisphere and three with right-hemisphere subdural grid implants, performing an instructed-delay reaching task on a touchscreen with each arm. The dataset repackages the authors' 1000 Hz exports in BIDS together with reach kinematics (position, speed, and angles). It supports investigation of hemispheric asymmetry in the encoding of bilateral arm kinematics in the human brain.
methods_description: Patients with subdural grids and strips were recorded at UCI and CPMC (Nihon Kohden) and at UCSF (Tucker Davis Technologies). Signals not recorded at 1000 Hz were low-pass filtered at 500 Hz and downsampled to 1000 Hz. Patients performed two blocks of 40 instructed-delay reaching trials per arm in counterbalanced order. Kinematics were estimated from button and touch times and are provided at 100 Hz. Neural data are stored as float32 BrainVision files and kinematics as physio TSV files.
